title: The service table shows Service, Interval, Canned Lines and reorders
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in, on the build under test, as an Owner/Admin or as a user with "Settings Service" enabled.
  2. In the left sidebar under Settings, open the "Maintenance" entry beneath "Inspection Templates" (if the build shows "Maintenance schedules" instead, use that entry and record the label). Schedules are shared by the whole organization, whichever location is chosen in the header.
  3. A schedule open in the editor with two services. Seed it:
  4. ↳ New schedule; Add service "PM-A": calendar Every 3 months, tick Distance and enter Every 15,000 (mileage); add 3 canned lines; save the service.
  5. ↳ Add service "PM-C": calendar Every 12 months; at "Services also covered" pick PM-A (its 3 lines arrive marked "from PM-A"); add 1 more canned line of its own; save the service.
custom_steps:
1. Read the service table's column headers.
  2. Read the Interval cell of PM-A and the Canned Lines cell of PM-C.
  3. Reorder the services by drag, then with Move up / Move down.
  4. Add a third service ("PM-D", Every 12 months) and see where it lands in the table.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The table has three columns: Service, Interval and Canned Lines.
  • PM-A's Interval reads "15,000 mileage · 3 months" (a dot between triggers, never "or"); PM-C's Canned Lines reads "4 lines · 3 covered" (1 own line + 3 from PM-A = 4).
  • Services reorder by drag and by Move up / Move down.
  • The new service lands at the bottom of the table (design: the drag handle's tooltip says "New services land at the bottom.").

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780, story SV-10558 (S1, Create a maintenance schedule), Chunk 1 MR (Confluence 886931488) as edited 5 October 2026, S1 (The service table; S1-R9, S1-R10); Design board "Chunk 1.dc.html" (MR V2 Claude Design project, version of 6 October 2026), artboard D1 (drag-handle tooltip); read 6 Oct 2026.   • S1-R10: “Services will be reorderable by drag and by Move up / Move down”
